content: In the year King Uzziah died, what did Isaiah see?
explanation: His robe filled the temple. “In the year that King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord seated on a throne, high and exalted” (Isaiah 6:1, BSB)
tags: Isaiah Sees the Lord on His Throne

content: In Isaiah's vision of the Lord's throne, how many wings did each seraph have?
explanation: They covered faces and feet, and flew. “Above Him stood seraphim, each having six wings” (Isaiah 6:2, BSB)
tags: Isaiah Sees the Lord on His Throne

content: In Isaiah's vision, what did the seraphim call out about the LORD?
explanation: The earth is full of His glory. “Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of Hosts; all the earth is full of His glory.” (Isaiah 6:3, BSB)
tags: Isaiah Sees the Lord on His Throne

content: Seeing the LORD on His throne, what did Isaiah cry?
explanation: He knew his lips were unclean. “Woe is me, for I am ruined” (Isaiah 6:5, BSB)
tags: Isaiah Sees the Lord on His Throne

content: In Isaiah's vision, what did a seraph bring from the altar?
explanation: He took it with tongs. “and in his hand was a glowing coal that he had taken with tongs from the altar.” (Isaiah 6:6, BSB)
tags: Isaiah Sees the Lord on His Throne

content: In Isaiah's vision, where did the seraph touch him with the coal?
explanation: His sin was atoned for. “And with it he touched my mouth” (Isaiah 6:7, BSB)
tags: Isaiah Sees the Lord on His Throne

content: When the Lord asked, “Whom shall I send?” what did Isaiah answer?
explanation: He was willing to go. “And I said: “Here am I. Send me!”” (Isaiah 6:8, BSB)
tags: Isaiah Sees the Lord on His Throne

content: In Isaiah's sign, the virgin's son would be called what?
explanation: Immanuel means God with us. “and will call Him Immanuel.” (Isaiah 7:14, BSB)
tags: A Child Is Born to Us

content: Isaiah says the Lord will give a sign: who will give birth to a son?
explanation: Matthew says this was fulfilled in Jesus. “Behold, the virgin will be with child and will give birth to a son” (Isaiah 7:14, BSB)
tags: A Child Is Born to Us

content: In Isaiah, what have the people walking in darkness seen?
explanation: Light dawned on them. “The people walking in darkness have seen a great light” (Isaiah 9:2, BSB)
tags: A Child Is Born to Us

content: Isaiah says, “For unto us a child is born, unto us a…”
explanation: The government will be on His shoulders. “For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given” (Isaiah 9:6, BSB)
tags: A Child Is Born to Us

content: In Isaiah's prophecy of the child, which is one of His names?
explanation: Also Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God. “And He will be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.” (Isaiah 9:6, BSB)
tags: A Child Is Born to Us

content: In Isaiah's prophecy, on whose throne will the promised child reign?
explanation: His kingdom will have no end. “He will reign on the throne of David and over his kingdom” (Isaiah 9:7, BSB)
tags: A Child Is Born to Us

content: In Isaiah's prophecy, of the increase of the child's government and peace there will be what?
explanation: His reign is forever. “Of the increase of His government and peace there will be no end.” (Isaiah 9:7, BSB)
tags: A Child Is Born to Us

content: In Isaiah, the suffering Servant is called a man of what?
explanation: He was despised and rejected. “He was despised and rejected by men, a man of sorrows, acquainted with grief.” (Isaiah 53:3, BSB)

content: In Isaiah, for what was the suffering Servant pierced?
explanation: He suffered in our place. “But He was pierced for our transgressions” (Isaiah 53:5, BSB)

content: In Isaiah, by the suffering Servant's stripes we are what?
explanation: His punishment brought us peace. “and by His stripes we are healed.” (Isaiah 53:5, BSB)

content: In Isaiah, we all like what have gone astray?
explanation: Each turned to his own way. “We all like sheep have gone astray” (Isaiah 53:6, BSB)

content: In Isaiah, the suffering Servant was led like what to the slaughter?
explanation: He did not open His mouth. “He was led like a lamb to the slaughter” (Isaiah 53:7, BSB)

content: In Isaiah, what did the suffering Servant do when oppressed?
explanation: He was silent like a sheep. “He was oppressed and afflicted, yet He did not open His mouth.” (Isaiah 53:7, BSB)

content: In Isaiah, what did the suffering Servant carry for us?
explanation: He took on our weakness. “Surely He took on our infirmities and carried our sorrows” (Isaiah 53:4, BSB)

content: In Isaiah, though your sins are like scarlet, they will be as white as what?
explanation: God offers cleansing. “Though your sins are like scarlet, they will be as white as snow” (Isaiah 1:18, BSB)

content: In Isaiah's vision of peace, what will nations beat their swords into?
explanation: No more training for war. “They will beat their swords into plowshares” (Isaiah 2:4, BSB)

content: In Isaiah, from whose stump will a shoot spring up?
explanation: Jesse was David's father. “Then a shoot will spring up from the stump of Jesse” (Isaiah 11:1, BSB)

content: In Isaiah's vision of peace, the wolf will live with what?
explanation: A little child will lead them. “The wolf will live with the lamb” (Isaiah 11:6, BSB)

content: In Isaiah, the LORD GOD is my strength and my what?
explanation: He has become my salvation. “For the LORD GOD is my strength and my song” (Isaiah 12:2, BSB)

content: In Isaiah, whom will God keep in perfect peace?
explanation: A steadfast mind finds peace. “You will keep in perfect peace the steadfast of mind, because he trusts in You.” (Isaiah 26:3, BSB)

content: In Isaiah, what does the voice calling in the wilderness say?
options: Prepare the way for the LORD
explanation: John the Baptist fulfilled this. “Prepare the way for the LORD in the wilderness” (Isaiah 40:3, BSB)

content: In Isaiah, the grass withers, but what stands forever?
explanation: God's word never fails. “The grass withers and the flowers fall, but the word of our God stands forever.” (Isaiah 40:8, BSB)

content: In Isaiah, those who wait on the LORD will mount up with wings like what?
explanation: They will renew their strength. “they will mount up with wings like eagles” (Isaiah 40:31, BSB)

content: In Isaiah, why does God tell His people not to fear?
explanation: He will strengthen and help. “Do not fear, for I am with you” (Isaiah 41:10, BSB)

content: In Isaiah, God tells Israel, “I have called you by your…”
explanation: You are Mine! “I have called you by your name; you are Mine!” (Isaiah 43:1, BSB)

content: In Isaiah, God's ways are higher than ours as the heavens are higher than what?
explanation: His thoughts are not our thoughts. “For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so My ways are higher than your ways” (Isaiah 55:9, BSB)

content: In Isaiah, if we are the clay, what is God?
explanation: We are the work of His hand. “we are the clay, and You are the potter” (Isaiah 64:8, BSB)

content: In Isaiah, the Spirit-anointed one preaches good news to whom?
explanation: Jesus read this in Nazareth. “because the LORD has anointed Me to preach good news to the poor.” (Isaiah 61:1, BSB)

content: Who was the prophet Isaiah's father?
explanation: Isaiah saw visions about Judah. “that Isaiah son of Amoz saw” (Isaiah 1:1, BSB)

content: What was the name of the son Isaiah took to meet King Ahaz?
explanation: They met at the upper pool. “Go out with your son Shear-jashub to meet Ahaz” (Isaiah 7:3, BSB)

content: In Isaiah, which king does God call “My shepherd”?
explanation: He would let Jerusalem be rebuilt. “who says of Cyrus, ‘My shepherd will fulfill all that I desire,’” (Isaiah 44:28, BSB)

content: In Isaiah, where does God say He has inscribed His people?
options: On the palms of His hands
explanation: He never forgets them. “Behold, I have inscribed you on the palms of My hands” (Isaiah 49:16, BSB)

content: Which Assyrian king attacked Judah's cities in Hezekiah's reign?
explanation: It was Hezekiah's fourteenth year. “Sennacherib king of Assyria attacked and captured all the fortified cities of Judah.” (Isaiah 36:1, BSB)

content: In Isaiah, the suffering Servant was assigned a grave with the wicked and with whom in death?
explanation: Jesus was buried in a rich man's tomb. “and with a rich man in His death” (Isaiah 53:9, BSB)

content: In Isaiah's vision, the lame will leap like what?
explanation: Streams will flow in the desert. “Then the lame will leap like a deer” (Isaiah 35:6, BSB)

content: In Isaiah, God says He will comfort His people as who comforts her son?
explanation: God's love is tender. “As a mother comforts her son, so will I comfort you” (Isaiah 66:13, BSB)

content: In Isaiah, which region is called Galilee of the what?
explanation: Light would dawn there. “Galilee of the nations” (Isaiah 9:1, BSB)
